title: Reading comprehension: the lighthouse keeper
text:
For thirty years, Joseph kept the lighthouse on a rocky island off the Konkan coast. Every evening he climbed the hundred and twelve steps, cleaned the great lens and lit the lamp before the sun touched the sea. Fishing boats returning after dark steered by its beam, and on stormy nights it was the only thing between them and the rocks.

When the lamp was made automatic, Joseph was told that his work was no longer needed. Visitors expected him to be bitter. Instead he spoke of the lighthouse as a colleague who had simply been promoted. "The light never belonged to me," he said. "It belonged to the boats. If it can now look after them without me, then my work was well done."

He still lives in the village on the mainland. On clear evenings he walks to the end of the jetty and waits, not for any ship, but for the moment the beam first sweeps across the water. Only then does he go home for his supper.

title: Reading comprehension: the water channels of a mountain village
text:
In a high, dry valley of the Himalaya, almost no rain falls in summer, yet the village fields are green. The water comes from a glacier above the village, carried down in narrow channels dug along the hillside. Each family's field receives water in turn, by a schedule agreed long ago and remembered without being written down.

The channels need constant care. A single rockfall can block one, and an untended breach can wash away a season's work in an afternoon. Every spring, before sowing, one person from each household joins the work of clearing them. No one is paid; the reward is water for the year. Families that do not send a worker are not punished, but they find that neighbours are slow to help them later.

Older villagers worry that the glacier is shrinking and that young people now leave for jobs in the towns. Yet the spring clearing still goes on, and each year the first water to reach the lowest field is greeted with a small celebration.
